pages.text: Every electric block has a $(item)maximum voltage$(), $(item)1,000 V$() by default, and some also have a $(item)maximum current$(). While a block is over its limit, a damage counter rises every half second. After a few seconds of overload, and even short overloads count, the block is $(item)destroyed and drops nothing$(). The block is lost for good.
A multimeter shows a red warning once a block reaches $(item)80%$() of a limit. Check new setups before you leave them running.

$(l)Blocks with higher voltage limits$()$(li)Cable hubs: 5,000 V$(li)Cable tubes, electric posts, stators and the large generator rotor: 10,000 V$(li)Insulators, diagonal cables, large switch and large transformer: 100,000 V
$(l)Current limits$()$(li)Lamps and neon tubes: 1 A$(li)Diode, switch, potentiometer and transformer: 100 A$(li)Freezer and electrode holder: 400 A$(li)Large transformer: 500 A, large switch: 1,000 A
A large generator can go well above 1,000 V. Step it down before it reaches ordinary machines.
